body: This sounds a bit AI, might be worth a human readable explanation?

Sorry, but I wrote this myself :P 

I'm not sure how to phrase it to be short while still being correct.

We are becoming one with the clanker.

How about this?

> Define out-of-class so it can be placed in the zero-fill region (.bss) instead of the initialized data section (.data). Because the zero-fill region is allocated at runtime, this reduces the binary size on disk and improves startup performance by avoiding redundant drive I/O.

actually might be worth saying to avoid `static inline`:

> Defined out-of-class instead of using static inline so the compiler can place the table in the zero-fill region (.bss) instead of the initialized data section (.data). Because the zero-fill region is allocated at runtime, this shrinks the binary size on disk and improves startup performance by avoiding redundant drive I/O.

or

> Defined out-of-class rather than using static inline. This allows the table to live in the zero-fill .bss region instead of the .data section, saving binary space on disk and speeding up startup by letting the OS allocate the zeroed memory at runtime.

Not sure which is best. :thinking: 
But Mach-0 sounds like a fighter plane, and that link is both long and made no sense. :blush:
I don't have a strong preference; i adapted your second version (no measurable startup performance improvement is expected so i removed that part).
